title: Enhancing Contract Negotiations with LLM-Based Legal Document Comparison
organization: JPMorgan Chase Machine Learning Center of Excellence
key_contributions: LLM-based approach for comparing legal contracts with templates using Natural Language Inference (NLI)
Bidirectional entailment testing: template concepts against contract, and contract concepts against template
Clause variation analysis to generate approved contract term catalog
RAG pipeline for clause library and amendment tracking
Achieves 96.46% accuracy on private real-world legal dataset

methodology.core_idea: Frame document comparison as document-level NLI: test whether template concepts are entailed/contradicted/neutral by contract document
methodology.bidirectional: Test both directions to catch additions (concepts in contract not in template) and deletions (concepts in template not in contract)
key_datasets: Internal JPMorgan contracts (25 master contracts, 5 with amendments, span 2007-2023)

direct_implication_for_skill: NLI framing is well-suited for regulatory/normative version comparison. Bidirectional testing (old→new AND new→old) naturally captures both scope_narrowed and scope_broadened changes. Current skill uses unidirectional comparison; consider adopting bidirectional pattern.
practical_outcome: Generated clause libraries suggesting template modifications, supported prenegotiated MSAs, accelerated contract review and negotiation timelines
resolution_requirement_for_downstream: Bidirectional comparison enables automatic detection of: (1) requirements no longer implied (narrowed scope), (2) requirements newly required (broadened scope). Downstream evidence must verify against both old and new requirements.
reading_notes: Pay attention to Section 4 (motivation and methodology). The NLI framing and bidirectional pattern are directly applicable to the version-delta skill. Consider implementing bidirectional testing in next iteration.
